items.titulo: Eli Lilly scraps phase 2 Alzheimer's program after drug falls short of expectations

items.titulo: Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
items.resumen: Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to strengthen its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.

items.resumen: Bristol Myers Squibb has scrapped a phase 1 program it bet $80 million on just two years ago.

items.resumen: BioMarin is paying $70 million upfront to license a Fabry disease drug candidate, expanding the franchise it acquired through its $4.8 billion takeover of Amicus Therapeutics.

items.titulo: Flagship brings 3 biotech platforms together to launch AI drug discovery player Etcelera

items.titulo: Why researchers may have found the biological culprit behind Angelman syndrome

items.titulo: Genmab's $8B Merus bet delivers as bispecific combo halves risk of death in phase 3
items.resumen: Capping off a busy few days in Spain, Genmab reported results from the first interim analysis of a phase 3 trial showing that adding its bispecific antibody petosemtamab to Merck & Co.'s Keytruda cut the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone in patients with PD-L1-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
